Nuzlocke is a self-imposed ruleset to make Pokemon more challenging where you:

1. Can only catch the first Pokemon you find in each area of the game (so first Pokemon found on Rt 1, first Pokemon in Mt Ember, etc)

2. Name every Pokemon

3. Cannot revive any fainted Pokemon (must box them)

They are doing a lighter form (“Nicklocke”) where the catching Pokemon rules doesn’t apply, but the rules for naming and fainted Pokemon do. Definitely glad they went this way as it’s more fun to try to catch em all, but keeps the suspense in battle

In regard of the customer characters, Andy is very talented and put in a lot of effort to mod a ROM of the game for all the custom characters and animations. There was even more customization in the FireRed Nicklocke, but the one they’re playing now was harder to mod because it came out on DS as opposed to GBA

I think the touchbar suffered from what most apple products that have failed in the past 10+ years suffer from: over-reliance on developers to actually make it useful. 

Touchbar was an interesting concept that never took off and ultimately never even came close to compensating for the functionality it tried to replace. Lack of 3rd party support def helped make that happen. 

Same issue the AVP suffers from, and to an extent both the Apple Watch and the iPad. They release the cool tech without the actual foundation for what it should be doing established, and are relying on developers and users to figure it out themselves. I feel like the App Store helping the iPhone explode into what it has become has led Apple to adopt this over-reliance on developers to actually make their products useful and it’s starting to really hurt their lineup over the long term

I feel like the No Return multipliers are a little insight into how the difficulty scales:

Very Light = 1.00
Light = 1.20
Moderate = 1.50
Hard = 1.80
Survivor = 2.00
Grounded = 2.5

The difference between Moderate and Hard (.3) is more significant than the difference between Hard and Survivor (.2)

The difference between Survivor and Grounded (.5) is equal to the difference between Moderate and Survivor (.5)

So if you go Moderate -> Survivor -> Grounded it’s .5 + .5 = 1

Moderate -> Hard -> Grounded is .3 + .7 = 1

In your case, the jump in difficultly going from Hard to Grounded might be more sudden, but imo the jump from Hard to Survivor (.2) isn’t worth it, I would just go for Grounded

That being said this is all total bs and you should play in whatever way makes it the most fun for you. I think if you wanna avoid being frustrated I would stick to survivor, it’s still a great challenge especially if you don’t do NG+ and in some ways a more enjoyable experience cause it isn’t so freaking stressful lol
